title: qLDPC code submission
description: A single qLDPC code submission: a CSS code given by its X and Z parity checks, or (schema 0.4) a general stabilizer code given by one list of Pauli generators. Parity checks are given as sparse supports (lists of qubit indices). Distance claims must carry a self-certifying witness operator for the upper-bound tier.

code_type.description: CSS: checks.X and checks.Z, per-side distance witnesses. stabilizer (schema 0.4): checks.S, one list of Pauli generators, and a single Pauli-weight distance witness distance.P. A code whose every generator is pure X or pure Z, or becomes so under single-qubit Cliffords on some qubits, is a CSS code and must be typed CSS (as that image); the verifier rejects it otherwise. The two types are ranked on separate leaderboards.

n.description: number of physical (data) qubits; capped by the verification-budget rule: 700 for any code, 1000 when max check weight <= 8 and claimed d <= 40 (enforced by the verifier, see qldpc_verify.admissible)

k.description: claimed number of logical qubits; verifier recomputes exactly

checks.description: CSS: X and Z (required, S forbidden). stabilizer: S (required, X and Z forbidden). The if/then rules below enforce the split by code_type.

distance.description: CSS: a claimed d needs witnesses for both sides (X and Z) to certify the upper bound, and d = min(dX, dZ). stabilizer: one Pauli-weight side P, and d = P.value.

d.description: claimed code distance: min(dX, dZ) for a CSS code, P.value for a stabilizer code

circuit.description: optional circuit tier (RFC 0001, issue #505): the entry ships syndrome-extraction memory circuits under circuits/<slug>/ (memory_x.stim, memory_z.stim, plus their derived .dem files), and claims a witness-backed circuit-level distance per basis. Penalty-only: the recorded d_circ is clamped to <= d and can only discount a score, never inflate it. Forbidden on stabilizer entries: the memory experiments are per basis, and a general stabilizer code needs a schedule the tier does not yet build.

d_circ.description: per-basis circuit-level distance of the memory experiments. Basis S is the S-basis memory circuit (circuits/<slug>/memory_<s>.stim): its witness is an undetected fault set flipping a logical-S observable. The effective d_circ = min(X.value, Z.value).

rounds.description: noisy extraction rounds in each memory circuit; the verifier requires rounds >= the claimed code distance d

stim_version.description: stim version that derived the committed .dem files; the verifier requires it to equal the version pinned in uv.lock and re-derives the .dem mechanism-for-mechanism (probabilities only to float tolerance: their last ulps are architecture-sensitive and the distance tier never reads them)

ancilla_coordinates.description: one [x, y] per non-data qubit in circuit index order (qubits n..total-1); required only for the geometric circuit tier (Phase B)

contributed_by.description: who contributed these circuits, and when. Schedule credit lives here, on the artifact contributed, not in provenance.authors, so contributing a circuit tier to an existing entry never changes its author list (issue #611). Required when the contributor is not a listed author of the code: verify/check_authorship.py binds such a PR through this field.

ler.description: optional measured logical-error-rate tier: the same committed memory circuits, sampled under the canonical noise recipe at one or more physical rates and decoded with the pinned decoder. Distance is a floor; this is the measured rate a device-like simulation actually sees, prefactors included. Since 0.5 each basis is a list of points (a curve), compared across entries only at equal p.

items.description: one measured point: the committed memory circuit, its canonical noise recipe re-applied at physical rate p, sampled and decoded with the pinned decoder. Self-reported measurement; CI re-measures with an independent seed (verify/ler_verify.py): the highest-rate point at PR time, the rest weekly post-merge with receipts under receipts/ler/.

p.description: physical rate of the canonical noise recipe, on the board's grid so points are comparable across entries at equal p; a point whose per-shot failure fraction exceeds 1/2 is saturated and rejected

shots.description: sampled shots; the floor keeps a claim statistically meaningful

failures.description: shots where the decoder's predicted observable flips disagreed with the sampled ones; at least 100, so the claim carries ~10% statistical error and prefactor comparisons between schedules are resolvable (raise shots until the count is reached)

seed.description: stim sampler seed; with shots and the pinned stim version this determines the sample

decoder.description: the pinned decoder (BP+OSD, minimum-sum, scaling 0.625, osd_cs order 10, 30 iterations, DEM-prob channel prior)

ler_per_round.description: per-round logical error rate via the parity-aware conversion from failures/shots and circuit.rounds

ci95.description: Wilson 95% interval on ler_per_round, from the same conversion

oneOf.description: schema 0.5 (issue #1278): a list of points, one per physical rate, highest rate first by convention. Distinct rates; the verifier replicates the highest rate at PR time and defers the rest to the weekly post-merge replication.
pre-0.5 form: one point at the canonical rate 0.001. Accepted on entries that declare schema 0.4 or earlier; a 0.5 entry carries the list form (verify/ler_verify.py checks the pairing).

logicals.description: a symplectic logical basis for the transversal-gate claims in `gates` (issue #1850): k X-type and k Z-type logical representatives, given as sparse supports, with X_i and Z_j anticommuting exactly when i = j. The gate claims name these operators as X0..X{k-1} and Z0..Z{k-1}. Verified: each X_i lies in ker(H_Z), each Z_i in ker(H_X), and the pairing matrix is the identity over GF(2), which also makes the basis independent modulo the stabilizers.

gates.description: claimed transversal logical gates (issue #1850, stage 1). Each is a qubit permutation, optionally with one single-qubit Clifford applied uniformly to every qubit (H or S), or a block-to-block CX between two copies of the code, together with the claimed action on the logical operators of `logicals`. The verifier checks over GF(2) that the gate maps every stabilizer generator into the stabilizer group (for S also that every X-check has weight 0 mod 4, the phase condition the GF(2) image cannot see) and that the induced action on each logical generator equals the claim up to stabilizers. Witness-backed and penalty-only: a verified gate is listed on the code page and never ranks; a wrong claim fails verification.

locality.description: optional; required for the 2d-local tracks and for a geometric-efficiency score. Planar or 3D coordinates.

coordinates.description: one [x, y] (D = 2) or [x, y, z] (D = 3) per qubit, indexed 0..n-1; every point in a layout has the same dimension (the verifier rejects a mix). The declared dimension is the one the layout is checked and priced in: the 2D-local classes need planar coordinates, and a 3D layout is scored by the D = 3 geometric efficiency (TRACKS.md).

layers.description: physical layers (1 for a single layer, 2 for flip-chip bilayer); required whenever a layout is given

modules.description: optional (schema 0.3): one module id per qubit, indexed 0..n-1, for a layout split across hardware modules (multi-chip assemblies, interconnected flip-chip modules, photonically linked or shuttling zones). A non-negative integer per qubit; ids need not be contiguous. Membership is independent of the coordinates, so it applies to a layout of any dimension. The verifier requires an id for every qubit and reports the checks that span more than one module, the ports (distinct neighboring modules) per module, and the qubits per module; it earns the Layer-3 flag `modular` and changes no track or score.

interaction_radius.description: claimed max check diameter in the layout; verifier recomputes

contributed_by.description: who contributed this layout, and when. Layout credit lives here, on the artifact contributed, not in provenance.authors, so contributing a layout never widens edit rights over the code (issue #611).

benchmark.description: optional Tier B metadata for the Beat the Surface Code campaign (issues #4601 and #4603): one documented comparison of this entry against a surface-code baseline at matched logical count, under a stated hardware track, noise model, and decoder, with syndrome ancillas counted. Non-scoring: no track or ranking reads it. The schema holds the vocabulary and ranges; the verifier checks the block against the entry and the board (the candidate's data qubits equal n, every total is its data plus ancillas, the baseline exists on the board with at least this entry's k or is k rotated patches of the stated distance) and records the reading in computed.benchmark. Requires schema_version 0.6.

hardware_track.description: the hardware track of issue #4601 whose surface-code baseline this comparison uses

kind.description: circuit-level depolarizing is the campaign's common benchmark; a phenomenological or code-capacity comparison is recorded as such and does not support an operational claim (issue #4601)

p.description: physical error rate the comparison is made at

bias.description: dephasing bias eta = p_Z / p_X of a biased model; 1 when unbiased

description.description: the recipe in one line when kind alone does not pin it: which operations carry noise, idling, measurement, and reset errors

slug.description: a committed surface-code entry, codes/<slug>.json, encoding at least this entry's k; the verifier checks that it exists (benchmark_baseline_on_board, benchmark_baseline_k) and reads its n and k

patches.description: k independent rotated surface-code patches of distance d, one per logical qubit of this entry, k d^2 data qubits in all: the baseline for a k with no single-code entry

implementation.description: package and version, or repository @ commit

resources.description: physical resources of the two memory experiments; the verifier requires candidate.data_qubits = n (benchmark_candidate_data_qubits) and baseline.data_qubits equal to the baseline entry's n or to k d^2 (benchmark_baseline_data_qubits)

target.description: pL_target of the comparison: the rate both experiments are sized to reach

per.description: whether the rates are per syndrome round or per memory experiment

status.description: documented: reported by the submitter from their own simulation, produced as method states. A verified status, reproduced by the repository's own tooling, is reserved until that tooling exists (issue #4601, Level 2).

method.description: how the numbers were produced: simulator, schedule source, where the baseline's numbers come from, and where the write-up lives

contributed_by.description: who contributed this comparison, and when. Required when the contributor is not a listed author of the code: verify/check_authorship.py binds such a PR through this field, as it does for a layout or a circuit tier, so a donated comparison never widens edit rights over the code (issue #611).

origin.description: baseline: a published code seeded for comparison. submission: a code contributed through the challenge. Defaults to submission when omitted.

novelty.description: optional literature-novelty status for submitted codes. known_parameters means the [[n,k,d]] parameter set exists in the literature even if this entry improves weight, layout, or construction details. new_parameters is a submitter/reviewer claim, not a verifier-proved fact.

construction.description: how the code was built (family, polynomials, search, reference)

model.description: optional, self-reported: the AI model that produced the code, named to a specific version (e.g. 'Claude Opus 4.8', not a bare 'Claude'), or 'human'. Claimed, not verified -- there is no way to certify which model generated a result, but if one is named the verifier requires a version so the claim is reproducible. May also be a list when a code was produced by an ensemble of models rather than a single one; the site joins them for display.

date.description: publication date for a literature baseline (a year is enough) or submission date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a contribution

clifford_relabel_of.description: optional (issue #2802): the slug of a board entry this code is a Clifford image of, under a Clifford acting on blocks of qubits. Such an image has the same n, k and code space as its parent, so its distance was bought with check weight and its kd^2/n is not a construction result; the verifier checks that the named entry exists with the same n and k, refuses novelty new_parameters alongside it, and the site marks the entry. Declaring it is the submitter's duty: multi-qubit Clifford equivalence is not tested, only the single-qubit case is (is_css_up_to_local_clifford).

clifford_block_size.description: optional, with clifford_relabel_of: the block size m of the block-local Clifford that produced this entry from its parent.

search_budget.description: optional, self-reported (schema 0.3): what the search that produced this code cost. The verifier checks none of it (there is nothing trustless to check); it is recorded so the cost of a frontier-advancing code can be compared across entries and over time. Distinct from distance.X/Z.witness_provenance, which budgets the witness search for one operator, not the code search. All fields optional; report what you measured and leave the rest out.

candidates_screened.description: codes built and screened (k, CSS, weight, cheap distance surrogate) before this one was chosen

ris_trials_per_side.description: deepest RIS budget spent per side on this code's distance during the search, in trials

cpu_hours.description: CPU core-hours over the whole search

gpu_hours.description: GPU-hours over the whole search (0 when none were used)

llm_tokens.description: tokens consumed per model, keyed by the model name as in provenance.model (e.g. {"Claude Opus 4.8": 1800000}); input and output combined

wall_clock_hours.description: elapsed time from the start of the search to this code

notes.description: what the numbers cover and what they leave out

family.description: construction family (Layer 2). Self-declared, since it cannot be recovered from H, and used only as a filterable tag, never for ranking. Topological covers surface/toric/color (say which in provenance.construction). See TRACKS.md. The listed examples are the established vocabulary and should be reused where they fit, since the site filters on them. A construction that genuinely does not fit may use a new lowercase-hyphenated tag rather than being flattened into 'other'; please open an issue so the vocabulary and the site's labels can follow.

tracks.description: deprecated and ignored for ranking. Track membership (the locality and weight classes) is computed by the verifier from H and the layout; this self-declared field is retained only for backward compatibility. See TRACKS.md.

allOf.$comment: a document using witness_provenance (a 0.2 feature) must declare schema_version 0.2 or later, so the version field stays meaningful rather than decorative
locality.contributed_by (a 0.2 feature) likewise requires schema_version 0.2 or later
the circuit tier is likewise a 0.2 feature
locality.modules (a 0.3 feature) requires schema_version 0.3 or later
provenance.search_budget (a 0.3 feature) requires schema_version 0.3 or later
a CSS entry carries checks.X/checks.Z and distance.X/distance.Z, never checks.S or distance.P
a stabilizer entry (a 0.4 feature) carries checks.S and distance.P, never checks.X/Z or distance.X/Z, has no circuit block, and declares schema_version 0.4
the benchmark block (a 0.6 feature, issue #4603) requires schema_version 0.6 or later

contributedBy.description: credit for one contributed artifact (a layout, a circuit tier). It sits on the artifact rather than in provenance.authors -- the same separation witness_provenance uses for refutation credit -- so a contribution never widens the contributor's edit rights over the code (issue #611).

by.description: @handles of the people who contributed this artifact

method.description: optionally, how the artifact was found (tool, model, search method)

value.description: claimed circuit-level distance for this basis; must equal |witness| and be <= the code distance d

confidence.description: the circuit tier currently has no exact certification path (MILP over H_dem is deferred future work), so every claim is a witness-backed upper bound

witness.description: sorted 0-based indices of error(...) instructions in this basis's committed flattened .dem, counted in file order. The XOR of their detector sets must vanish (undetected) and the XOR of their observable sets must not (flips a logical): the circuit-tier analogue of the low-weight logical the code tier stores.

supportList.description: one entry per parity check; each entry is the sorted list of distinct qubit indices in that check's support

confidence.description: upper_bound: self-certified by the witness. exact: also requires server certification; treated as upper_bound until confirmed.

witness.description: support of a nontrivial logical operator of this Pauli type achieving `value`. X-witness lives in ker(H_Z) and outside rowspace(H_X); Z-witness mirrors.

operatorList.description: a list of Pauli operators of one type, each the sorted list of distinct qubit indices in its support (no per-operator weight cap: logical representatives can be heavier than a check)

transversalGate.description: one claimed transversal logical gate. `gate` is `permutation` (a bare qubit permutation, which must then be given), `H` or `S` (that Clifford on every qubit, composed with the optional permutation), `CX` (a CX from qubit i of one block, the control, to qubit permutation[i] of a second block, the target; identity pairing when omitted), or `match` (issue #2894: a W<=2 diagonal layer, `clifford` S on the qubits of `support` with CZ on the disjoint matching `pairs`, or SHS on the support with CZ# = (H x H) CZ (H x H) on the matching; no permutation). `logical_action` maps each logical generator label to the list of generator labels whose product it is sent to, checked up to stabilizers only (a logical factor the gate introduces belongs in this list); a generator not listed is claimed fixed. Labels are X0..X{k-1}, Z0..Z{k-1} for the (control) block and X0'..Z{k-1}' for the target block of a CX.

permutation.description: image of each qubit: qubit i is sent to permutation[i]; must be a permutation of 0..n-1

clifford.description: match only: the single-qubit gate applied on `support`, which fixes the entangler on `pairs` (S with CZ, both Z-diagonal; SHS with CZ#, both X-diagonal)

support.description: match only: the qubits the single-qubit gate acts on (distinct, below n; may be empty when `pairs` is not)

pairs.description: match only: the entangler's qubit pairs, a matching (no qubit in two pairs, endpoints distinct and below n); a qubit may be in both `support` and a pair

name.description: optional display label, e.g. 'logical Hadamard' or 'SWAP of logical qubits 0 and 1'

witnessProvenance.description: who found this witness, when, and at what search budget (issue #611). Refutation credit lives here, on the operator contributed, not in provenance.authors; the budget a bound has survived is what tells the next refuter what they need to beat.

found_by.description: @handles of the people who found (or, for a surviving bound, deep-tested) this witness

found_at_samples.description: the search budget this witness was found at. Says nothing about whether something lighter exists.

survived_samples.description: the largest budget a deep search has spent on this side WITHOUT finding anything lighter than this witness. Only a null result may write this; it is the number that actually constrains the distance, and it is what a later refuter needs to beat.

generatorList.description: one entry per stabilizer generator of a general stabilizer code: the generator X^{X} Z^{Z}, given by the sorted list of distinct qubit indices carrying an X factor and the sorted list carrying a Z factor. A qubit in both lists carries Y. Row i of the binary symplectic matrix S = (A | B) is (indicator of X | indicator of Z). At least one list is nonempty; the check weight is the size of the union of the two lists.

pauliSideDistance.description: the single distance side of a general stabilizer code. There are no X and Z sides: d is the minimum Pauli weight over the nontrivial logical operators, and the witness is one Pauli operator of that weight.

value.description: claimed minimum Pauli weight of a nontrivial logical operator

confidence.description: upper_bound: self-certified by the witness. exact: accepted as upper_bound; the Pauli-weight certifier is not yet available.

witness.description: a nontrivial logical Pauli operator X^{X} Z^{Z} of Pauli weight `value` (a qubit in both lists is Y and counts once). It must commute with every generator and lie outside the row space of S.

resourceCount.description: physical resources of one memory experiment at the stated noise and target

ancilla_qubits.description: syndrome and flag qubits; 0 only for a comparison that counts data qubits alone, which method must say

rounds.description: syndrome rounds in the memory experiment

spacetime_volume.description: total_qubits x rounds unless method says otherwise

decoder_latency_us.description: mean decoding time per round in microseconds, on the hardware method names
